proposals.hypothesis: Li2Si2O5 is a silicate built on Si4+, which is very hard to reduce, so it should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl. It is a wide-gap electronic insulator that should be stable near 4 V vs Li. Its Li content is lower than the Li-rich silicates in the earlier proposals, but it is a chemically clean silicate test of the reduction-resistant Si4+ framework at the LiCoO2/Li6PS5Cl interface.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium phosphate that is well known as a protective coating for layered oxide cathodes. Its P5+ framework should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li, and it is a common buffer against sulfide electrolytes, so it is a reasonable first test for the LiCoO2/Li6PS5Cl interface.

Li3Al(BO3)2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium borate built from B3+ and Al3+, neither of which is easily reduced by Li6PS5Cl or oxidized at 4 V vs Li. It offers a chemically different borate framework from the earlier phosphate test, so it is a useful next probe of whether a non-phosphate oxide coating lowers the interfacial penalty at LiCoO2 and Li6PS5Cl.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 test (mp-aaaaaegs) established a phosphate-based baseline; this explores a different chemical family (borate) with a wide band gap and no reducible cations.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-rich fluoride with a highly stable anion (F-) that is thermodynamically resistant to oxidation at 4 V vs Li and to reduction by Li6PS5Cl. Its low solubility and lack of reducible cations make it a plausible buffer layer at the LiCoO2/Li6PS5Cl interface. It also comes from a halide family not yet tested, which broadens coverage beyond the phosphate and borate probes.
proposal.motivation: Earlier phosphate (Li3PO4) and borate (Li3Al(BO3)2) tests established baselines in those families; this explores an unrepresented halide family with a wide band gap and no reducible cations.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich oxide with O2- as the only anion. It should resist oxidation at 4 V vs Li and has no reducible cations, so it is a plausible buffer at the LiCoO2/Li6PS5Cl interface. It also comes from the other_oxide family, which has not been tested yet.
proposal.motivation: Earlier probes covered phosphate, borate, and halide coatings, so this picks an unrepresented oxide family to broaden coverage.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8SiO6 is a Li-rich orthosilicate with Si4+ as the only cation. Si4+ is very hard to reduce, so the phase should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl and oxidation at 4 V vs Li. It is expected to be a wide-gap electronic insulator. The silicate family has not been tested yet, so this broadens coverage beyond the phosphate, borate, halide and Li2O probes.
proposal.motivation: Earlier probes covered phosphate, borate, halide and simple-oxide coatings, so this picks the untested silicate family for a Li-rich, reduction-resistant, wide-gap coating.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a Li-rich orthoborate with B3+ as the only cation. B3+ is very hard to reduce, so the phase should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl, and it is expected to be a wide-gap electronic insulator that is stable against oxidation near 4 V vs Li. Its Li-rich composition should also support ionic conduction across the interface.

Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich aluminosilicate built from Al3+ and Si4+, neither of which is easily reduced by Li6PS5Cl or oxidized at 4 V vs Li. Its high Li content should support ionic transport across the LiCoO2/Li6PS5Cl interface, and it should be a wide-gap electronic insulator. It is a chemically distinct Li-rich silicate from the earlier silicate probe, so it tests whether the Al/Si framework with extra Li lowers the interfacial penalty.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li-rich silicate probe (Li8SiO6 proposal) and the other family tests set a silicate and Li-rich oxide baseline. This candidate keeps the reduction-resistant Si4+/Al3+ framework while adding Al and more Li to improve ionic conduction.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Si2O7 is a Li-rich silicate built on Si4+, which is very hard to reduce and so should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl. It should also be a wide-gap electronic insulator that is stable against oxidation near 4 V vs Li. Its high Li content should support ionic transport across the LiCoO2/Li6PS5Cl interface.
proposal.motivation: The earlier Li-rich silicate proposal (Li8SiO6 hypothesis) pointed to Si4+ frameworks with high Li content as reduction-resistant, insulating coatings. Li6Si2O7 is the closest available analog of that idea.

It keeps the reduction-resistant silicate framework from earlier hypotheses while adding Al and more Li than the stoichiometric LiAlSiO4 analogs.
